title: Phawar of the Family Hearth (Akor Shong Iing Shong Sem)
cultural_context: Rhyming maxims instructing family members on domestic harmony, filial piety, and hospitality around the clay hearth (*Rympei*), from 'Ka Jingsneng Tymmen'.

khasi: Ha iing ha sem to ai kan shong,
U kpa u trei da ka hok,
Ka kmie ka ri da ka jingieit;
Ki khun ki kohnguh da ka akor,
Hangta ka dpei ka syaid jai-jai,
Ha ka jingkmen ba u Blei u ai.
english: Within the family home let there dwell,
The father labors with honest sweat,
The mother nurtures with selfless love;
The children obey with graceful etiquette,
There the family hearth glows warm and bright,
Bathed in the joy bestowed by God.

khasi: Pdiang sngewbha ia uba wan kai,
Ai kwai, ai tympew da ka mynsiem ba shai;
Ka jingbha jong ka ling ka sem
Kam dei ha ka spah ba kynrei;
Hynrei ha ka akor bad ka hok,
Ba pynlong ia ka ling kum ka khet;
To ngin sumar ia kane ka tnum
Ba kan tyngshain ha la ka shnong.
english: Welcome the guest with a cheerful and generous countenance,
Offer betel nut and fresh leaf with an open, loving heart;
The true excellence of a home and household
Consists not in hoards of silver or gold;
Rather in upright decorum and integrity,
Transforming the humble dwelling into a royal throne;
Let us protect and preserve this ancestral roof
That it may shine as a light in our village.

vocabulary.kwai bad tympew: betel nut and betel leaf (sacred emblem of Khasi hospitality)
